local_checks.invariant: Ambiguous discovered site identities cannot reach configuration update through a stale capability or alternate handler.
local_checks.result: Discover normalizes and deduplicates names (discover.go:581-590), builds stable IDs from primary domain and configuration path (170), counts domains across files and removes update after managed-site classification (80-99). Manager.Update reacquires discovery under siteWriteMutex, requires the action, explicitly rejects ambiguous state, and checks resource version/collisions (manager.go:198-229,647-669). Both managed publication (271-275) and CLI publication (cli_update.go:59-65) rediscover before exchange; therefore stale UI capability does not bypass the new rejection. Agent PATCH reaches Manager.Update unless performing separate certificate-only replacement (agent/server.go:1153-1166). That sibling rejects simultaneous setting edits and binds the selected configuration to the exact canonical domain path plus version and certificate hashes (certificate_replace.go:55-114), so it is not a path to the server_name update prohibited here. Read the duplicate-domain test at discover_test.go:251; no test was run.

local_checks.invariant: A site delete request must bind the selected identity to its explicitly authorized destructive scope.
local_checks.result: Traced the retained delete action because the new discovery warning promises configuration-ID deletion. Actual DeleteWithOptions delegates to deleteWithScript (manager.go:368-373), which resolves the ID and rejects a mismatched normalized PrimaryDomain (script_delete.go:117-136), then deliberately runs domain-level k web del with fixed argv (75-80,161). Panel authenticates and requires origin/CSRF plus durable audit intent (panel/sites.go:247-290). The final dialog explicitly confirms deletion of that domain's directory, Nginx config, certificates and same-named database (SiteDeleteDialog.vue:33-41); existing tests explicitly require full domain deletion without resource version and reject domain mismatch (manager_test.go:264-317). Thus differing IDs sharing a domain do not establish an unauthorized action under the actual confirmation contract. The inaccurate resource-ID warning is recorded as hardening, not a vulnerability. External script behavior was not executed or assumed as validated.

local_checks.invariant: Audit migration, append, paging and password recovery must maintain private durable records, with failed storage represented as failure.
local_checks.result: Read complete new audit_log.go and all store/auth changed hunks plus consumers. Linux process lock excludes concurrent store owners; DB starts with 0600, a single connection, WAL/FULL sync, parameterized SQL, transactional append/trim, normal duplicate-ID rejection, closed/unlinked-file write checks, and page limit (audit_log.go:53-251; store.go:168-275). Audit reader is session-gated and returns storage errors (server.go:1019-1048). Password recovery appends before credential mutation and appends a failure record if state persistence fails (store.go:376-404). Existing interrupted-migration test only checks duplicate-free listing before a later append (audit_log_test.go:81-106); it does not settle sequence-gap retention. go.mod pins modernc.org/sqlite v1.55.0; no driver execution or external verification performed.

local_checks.invariant: Repeating an interrupted migration must not reduce the retained audit history when the next normal event is written.
local_checks.result: migrateAuditLocked explicitly repeats import after a crash between database commit and JSON cleanup (store.go:244-259). The table uses AUTOINCREMENT (audit_log.go:88-93), duplicate migration uses INSERT OR IGNORE (166-168), and pruning assumes contiguous sequence numbers (186-188). This creates the candidate sequence-gap data-loss path, pending exact-driver validation. An unauthenticated invalid login can append an audit event after the existing five-second global/one-minute source audit throttle allows it (server.go:681-683,864-889,1525-1530).

local_checks.invariant: Independent refutation of audit-migration-autoincrement-gap-retention-loss
local_checks.result: needs_validation: The store explicitly promises that restarting an interrupted audit migration does not lose records. Its database import commits separately from removal of the legacy JSON array. Replaying the migration uses INSERT OR IGNORE in an AUTOINCREMENT table, whereas later retention measures sequence distance rather than the number of retained events. If ignored inserts advance the persisted sequence in the pinned driver, a subsequent ordinary event can delete history that should remain within the 10000-event cap; after one replay at capacity the candidate result is loss of all 10000 previous events. An unauthenticated requester able to reach the login handler and pass its existing request controls can supply that subsequent event through an ordinarily permitted failed login. The attacker is not shown to cause or detect the interrupted migration. This is a conditional audit-integrity candidate, not a demonstrated remote erasure vulnerability or an observed database result.

local_checks.invariant: Moving process spawn outside the manager lock must preserve admission quotas, ownership and shutdown cleanup without blocking unrelated session reads.
local_checks.result: Open serializes admission with openSpawnMu, counts active owner/global sessions under mu, then releases mu only for spawn and checks closed both after spawn and before registration (manager.go:279-343). Failure/closed paths close and kill the returned process. Close retains identity/capacity on kill failure, serializes retries with closeMu, and does not hold item.mu across stop I/O (457-490); reap preserves failed-close state (520-537). Lookup binds owner (541-549). Panel derives owner from authenticated user and reserves concurrent opens before Agent dispatch (panel/terminal.go:139-221); Agent input/output sizes and waits remain bounded (agent/terminals.go:151-176; manager.go:17-24,386-455). Read new spawn/nonblocking regression at close_test.go:168 and existing failed-stop/retry tests; no tests or subprocesses were executed.

local_checks.invariant: A terminal spawn cannot evade host-backup mutation exclusion between process creation and session registration.
local_checks.result: Investigated the narrow window after spawning is cleared at manager.go:312 and before sessions registration at 342, during which a direct Manager.Busy caller could observe false. The reachable Agent requests cannot exploit that window: ServeHTTP holds backupMutationMu over the entire non-GET/HEAD handler, including terminal Open, and backup admission evaluates backupHostWorkersActive under the same mutex (agent/server.go:297-311; backup.go:3-6). A backup request therefore cannot race registration through the actual entrypoint. Busy includes all unclosed registered shells (manager.go:352-367), and the Agent separately permits close during backup. Existing backup gate test at agent/backup_test.go:24-65 was read only. Standalone manager bookkeeping can be hardened, but the complete source path refutes an exposed backup-admission vulnerability.
